body:

[Pacify] Final price for me was $77usd, minus hopefully 35% cashback from topcashback uk. Actual final price after cashback was $75aud, glad I didn't just buy the Asus one yesterday
Good timing, my ancient router finally gave up yesterday
[FrugalHoward] Was waiting for this one with all the coupon codes and paypal discounts for today. Cashback has tracked through TCB too. Thanks, Clear!
[squarepants] Did you do your cashback via TCB AU or UK, seeing as your cashback tracked in AUD?
[FrugalHoward] @squarepants: Through TCB AU. Paid in USD with PayPal.
[thingling] I used the coupon code, TCB UK but not PayPal/USD.
$120.83 paid, £21.84 cashback.
[Stonx] how long did it take to show the transaction on TCB UK?
I created an account and bought an hour ago, nothing yet under transaction but it did show the clicks
[SaveTheManuals] @Stonx: About 10 minutes for me. I also just created an account. Check you have verified your email too
[Stonx] @SaveTheManuals: I have verified the email. Maybe I'll wait till tomorrow before reaching to TCB support
[thingling] @Stonx: Took about 20 mins to show for me, was also a brand new account.
[SaveTheManuals] What code do we use to still be eligible for the cashback via TCB UK?
[SaveTheManuals] Update: Saw on the other posts that's people usually just use the AU codes
[squarepants] For the people doing cashback, is that through TCB UK as per OP?
[currentfad] yeah, just made an acc. But i forgot to use a referral code - think u get 2.5gbp bonus after earning 5gbp and referrer gets more.
[squarepants] Thanks both, I need to read up a bit on how this overseas cashback works.
[currentfad] I believe it's same as AU cashback sites. Payout either to bank acc or Paypal. If you have a Wise card you would just set up a virtual GBP acc and put those details in, then spend it as GBP (and let Wise do the spot rate conversion for you if you were making a transaction in AUD).
[padman] Have this and the 5GHZ band is very unstable. Anyone else with this issue?
[MrGareth] What firmware version are you running? I'm still on 4.8.3…. the newer versions apparently decreased the transmission power resulting in poorer wifi.
[xdirex] Can you install older versions? I think I’m on the latest but surprised my range isn’t quite what I expected in my cardboard home.
[sween64] No issues for me. Able to flog Steam downloads over 5 GHz from a floor up. Although my internet is capped around 550 Mbps down. Currently on firmware 4.9.0.
[asmith84] 5GHz was unstable on 4.9.0, so reverted back to 4.8.3. Installed 4.9.1 as soon as it was released, and it has been flawless since, 5GHz issue went away. Wireguard setup messed up during updates though so had to redo again.
[quick-dry] was the wireguard messup on the drop down to 4.8.3 though? If I recall there was a change in VPN priority policy configuration from 4.8.x to 4.9
I'm on 4.9 already and have a lot of devices already configured to connect to it's wireguard server so I don't want to risk buggering around with that for a minor upgrade to 4.9.1
[Torquecox] Price shows as $161usd on my account, $97usd if not logged in? any fixes or just make a new account?
[pdtmathieson] Got one of these recently, holy moly it’s improved my speed a lot. I didn’t have an easy time getting off my old router but got there in the end, config was messy
[Kefuan] Grabbed one to undated my Telstra smart modem 2…. 🙂
[Clear] Keep your smart modem. If you ditch Telstra they'll ask for it back and send you a bill if they don't get it.
[Kenciah] I should have patience and wait for this price drop, unfortunately, I just bought it 2 weeks ago. Honestly, I can't tell much difference between old router and this one. Maybe depend the use case, only watching netflix and wfh.
[bbtlovebbt] This kind of routers people normally using it with openwrt to do something tricky. Can't think up a case normal users use this kind of router for.
[mr_fjackson] Security updates ?
I have a Netgear router (Facebook market place) that was end of life 1 year before it was sold new, did it ever get any security updates? It's on a list of routers with known security vulnerabilities, I use it as a paperweight.
I expect openwrt will still be pushing out updates long after this device is Well and truly obsolete.
[Nashie069] Bought it last sale. Have 500/100 mbps connection and can get the full speed via wifi. Also have WiFi 6 throughout the house. Highly recommend!
[theUnderdog] How big is your house if you dont mind me asking
[ausduckz] Was going to pull the trigger during early bird sales, but thought against it and might wait 6-12 months.
[KillerkratZ] How does this work if I’m coming from a mesh system. Would I need to buy 2 for better coverage? Does this have some functionality to work together?
[Clear] GL.iNet haven't finished their mesh functionality. What mesh system do you have? It'll probably be better than this.
[mmd] Is the code valid if you go through topcashback AU?
[mmd] Legend thanks 👍
Going to order, thanks for the post.
[SaveTheManuals] Has anyone here used this and can they compare it to an Archer VR400? My current range is quite poor, and I need higher bandwidth at the front of the house to support a video doorbell. With the VR400, I only get a slow speed there, about 20 metres away through a wall.
[keijoh] I replaced my Archer VR400 with the Flint 2 around 6 months ago due to poor speeds at the back of my house. It solved my speed issues - able to get full speed now no issue. It’s probably a similar distance ~20m with 3 walls between the router and devices. YMMV
[Tarun Tuli] Sorry to be a pain, i have been with optus supplied router and mesh with 500 mb plan.
My use case is wfh with zoom calls, outlook ai eyc etc standard use
And netflix i get 500 mb throughout my house.
[JuiceWRLD] same, payment went through but then got a message saying items unavailable :(
[Clear] The store has added more stock. No idea how long it'll last.
[SnowDragon] Thanks - paid $77.26 USD. Bank shows $114.19 AUD.
Waiting for cashback to be tracked but I'm happy!
[SnowDragon] £19.98 pending cashback.
Brings the router down to about $78~ depending on conversion fees of cashback.

[Pacify] There's absolutely nothing rando about glinet routers, they been around a long time and generally considered one of the better choices for openwrt routers especially considering the price point
